title: Samoan oka with coconut cream

ingredients.note: very fresh tuna or other firm fish, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps: Use only very fresh fish bought from a trusted supplier. Keep it cold until you start.
Toss the fish cubes with the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Leave in the fridge for 10 to 15 minutes, until the outside turns opaque.
Drain off most of the lime juice. Mix in the onion, tomato, cucumber, spring onion and chilli, if using.
Stir in the coconut cream just before serving, taste and add more salt or lime. Serve well chilled.
notes: Curing time changes the texture: leave it longer if you prefer firmer, more opaque fish. Pregnant, elderly or immunocompromised people should avoid raw fish.

title: Oven-baked palusami

ingredients.note: fresh or frozen (thawed), stalks trimmed; use young leaves

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Cut six squares of foil about 30 cm wide and, if you have them, line each with a banana leaf.
Divide the taro leaves into six piles, overlapping the leaves to form a shallow cup in the middle of each square.
Mix the onion with a good pinch of salt and spoon into the cups. Pour about 65 ml of coconut cream into each.
Fold the leaves over the filling and wrap tightly in the foil, sealing the parcels well.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the leaves are completely soft and dark. Open carefully and serve hot, with the creamy juices.
notes: Taro leaves must be cooked thoroughly because raw leaves irritate the mouth and throat. Fresh young leaves are tender; frozen ones are easiest to find outside the Pacific. Traditionally the parcels are cooked in an umu.

title: Taro with coconut caramel sauce

ingredients.note: peeled and cut into large chunks

steps: Boil the taro in plenty of lightly salted water for 25 to 30 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain well.
Meanwhile, put the coconut cream, sugar and salt in a wide pan and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and slightly golden. Watch it near the end so it does not catch.
Serve the warm taro with the sauce poured over it.
notes: Taro must be cooked well, never eaten undercooked. Green bananas or breadfruit can be used in place of taro.

title: Coconut buns baked in coconut sauce
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, 50 g sugar and salt. Add the milk, egg and butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Knock back the dough and shape into 12 balls. Arrange them in a greased baking dish with a little space between.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 180 C.
Stir the coconut cream and 100 g sugar until the sugar dissolves, and pour over and around the buns.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden. Let them sit in the sauce for 10 minutes before serving warm.
notes: The sauce thickens as it cools, and the buns keep well for a day.

title: Samoan sapasui
steps: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes until soft, drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Heat the oil in a large pan or wok. Brown the beef over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then remove.
In the same pan, fry the onion, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes. Add the carrot and celery and fry for 3 minutes.
Return the beef, add the soy sauce and water and bring to a simmer.
Add the noodles and toss for 3 to 5 minutes until they absorb the liquid and turn glossy. Season and serve hot.
notes: Chicken can replace the beef. Add cabbage or spring onion if you like.

title: Oven-baked breadfruit
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C. Cut out the stem core of the breadfruit and make a few shallow cuts in the skin.
Wrap the whole breadfruit in foil and place on a tray.
Bake for 75 to 90 minutes, turning once, until a skewer slides through the centre with no resistance.
Let it cool for 10 minutes, then peel, remove the core and cut into thick wedges. Serve with salt or a little coconut cream.
notes: Mature but not fully ripe breadfruit is best for baking. Traditionally it is cooked directly on the hot stones of an umu.

title: Papaya in coconut milk

ingredients.note: ripe, peeled, seeded and cut into 2 cm chunks

steps: Put the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a pan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the papaya and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until soft but still holding its shape.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly thickened.
Serve warm in bowls.
notes: Use ripe but firm papaya. Adjust the sugar to the sweetness of the fruit.

title: Cocoa rice porridge
steps: Put the rice and water in a pot, bring to the boil, then reduce to a low simmer and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Whisk the cocoa with a few spoonfuls of the hot liquid to make a smooth paste, and stir it into the rice.
Add the sugar, salt and coconut milk. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Serve hot. It thickens as it cools, so loosen with a splash of water or coconut milk if needed.
notes: Traditionally made with Samoan cocoa balls (koko Samoa). Cocoa powder gives a milder version.

title: Slow-roasted pork, umu style

ingredients.note: large leaves, softened over a flame

steps: Heat the oven to 160 C. Score the pork skin and rub the salt thoroughly into the meat and skin.
Wrap the pork in banana leaf if using, then in two layers of foil, sealing tightly.
Roast on a tray for about 3 hours 30 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulling away from the bone.
Unwrap, increase the oven to 220 C and roast for 15 to 20 minutes more to crisp the skin.
Rest for 15 minutes, then carve and serve.
notes: A home oven cannot reproduce the smoky taste of an umu, but slow cooking in leaves and foil gives tender, moist meat.

title: Green bananas in coconut cream
steps: Cut the ends off the bananas and slit the skins lengthwise. Boil in lightly salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender.
Drain, cool slightly and peel off the skins. Cut into thick chunks.
Warm the coconut cream with a good pinch of salt in a pan, add the banana and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve hot, with the creamy sauce spooned over.
notes: Unripe bananas stain, so wear gloves or oil your hands if peeling many. Taro or breadfruit also work.
